games.notes: A separate game from game-3, but the SAME anchor (Infernal) — this one is Build Lab's own automatic recommendation rather than a Theory Craft build, Very Hard. Died around wave 50-51 with gold left in the bank. Owner's own diagnosis: poor elemental coverage and no second AoE main-dps; the lineup got 'rocked on fire as well as dark'. Root-cause investigation that session: Infernal's own top recommended package (blacksmith, doom, infernal, jinx, life-altar, root, shredder) already has adequate AoE and element coverage per lib/engine/buildPlanner.ts's own evidence. The real, confirmed mechanism is sequencing in lib/engine/buildProgression.ts's stepPriority (not buildPreferredKeystonePath, an earlier, wrong guess): its anchorPrerequisiteProgress term outranks actionPriority, so Darkness/Fire (Infernal's own recipe) keep winning keystones over Nature/Earth/Light (needed by Root/Shredder/Life Altar) until the anchor's whole recipe is spent, landing Light at wave 46 and Root's Nature-2 upgrade at wave 51. A live experiment reordering that priority was tried and made things WORSE (waves 36-55 went from about half failing to all failing) — Infernal's own single-target DPS at full level covers more total wave HP than a half-developed AoE spread under the model's current wave-HP curve, so that reorder was reverted; buildProgression.ts is unchanged. The fix actually applied instead, per the owner's direction to fix Build Lab's own ranking rather than reject in Match Plan: lib/engine/buildPlanner.ts's decisionVector and lib/engine/normalPackageSearch.ts's computeSearchDecisionVector now rank damage-shape (AoE) coverage above element-matchup coverage. This did not change Infernal's own package (already fine) but is the correct standing principle going forward. Auditing all 22 CURATED_ANCHORS afterward found a second, previously-unnoticed instance of the same defect: Laser's own recommended package (laser, doom, money, rage, tesla-tree) is entirely single-target with no AoE anywhere, and the ranking reorder alone did not fix it either — Laser needs its own investigation of the same depth as this one. With both real losses now confirmed as the same anchor, the wave-36-55 shortfall reads less like an Infernal-specific bug and more like a real, general weakness of the Infernal recipe against the model's current wave-HP curve — worth weighting accordingly the next time this anchor is tuned. Second attempt 2026-09-16: found and fixed a real, distinct bug in lib/engine/matchPlan.ts's allocationOrder — its element merge counted by element only, not position, so an early preference token (the anchor's own operational-level push, or the early-game coverage-element pick) could silently cash in a LATER, differently-positioned occurrence of the same element from buildProgression.ts's own (already well-ordered) serialized route, corrupting it. Fixed correctly this time (dequeuing the matching element from serialized's own list instead of double-counting) and verified against the full CURATED_ANCHORS audit rather than Infernal alone. Result: even though the fix visibly balanced Infernal's own Darkness/Fire completion and pulled Light/Nature/Earth earlier as intended, waves 36-50 got WORSE (new failures at W36-38, W43, W46-47 that were not there before) and it introduced a fresh regression elsewhere (haste banked 3,510g idle in Waves 36-40 with a wave still short). Reverted. This is now the THIRD independent confirmation (after the two stepPriority reorder attempts) that no keystone/allocation-order change can fix this — Infernal's own raw single-target DPS is simply the most HP-efficient lever available under the current wave-HP model, so anything that trades anchor completion time for earlier package-role coverage nets negative. The actual blocker is the wave-HP calibration gap tracked in tests/engine/matchPlanCalibration.test.ts (the model runs ~2x hot vs measured zero-leak wins) — until that has real data, sequencing work on this anchor should stop.

hpCalibration.note: Root-cause audit at the owner's request found the waves-1-55 creep HP curve (normalHp() in lib/engine/waveBenchmarks.ts) was an undocumented, unsourced exponential fit that credited 119.0M total creep HP through wave 55 on Hard, against only 66.0M (Bloom, zero-leak win through wave 61) and 50.1M (Wisp, zero-leak win through wave 59) actually dealt in the two archived real wins — a computed 1.80x and 2.38x overshoot respectively (verified directly, not assumed). This was proven independent of any tower-damage modeling: the check sums only the HP curve against real screenshotted totals. Applied HP_CALIBRATION_SCALE = 1/3 to the waves-1-55 curve only (boss-stage HP at wave56+ is untouched, since BOSS_BASE_HP=500,000 is sourced from the developer workbook directly, not invented). This is an explicit placeholder pinned to the only two real data points available, not a claim of the true per-wave shape; replace it the moment real per-wave HP or creep-count captures exist. After the fix, all three previously-it.fails calibration assertions in tests/engine/matchPlanCalibration.test.ts pass for real and were flipped to plain it; the 22-anchor doctrine audit and a 6-archetype spot check (infernal, laser, bloom, wisp, disease, haste) all clear every wave 1-55 at both Hard and Very Hard, with only the untouched boss stage (56-70) still showing shortfall, a separate known gap.
